summary: mypintusan gains the groups/schedules/grants surface that was the missing half of access control: until now a person created through the first-run wizard could not badge through any door, because the fail-closed decision path requires a Grant and nothing served one. A new apps/mypintusan/apis/access_rules.go exposes GET/POST /api/groups (+ /api/groups/{id}/members add/remove, with holder names hydrated so the screen never shows a raw id), GET/POST /api/schedules with embedded weekly windows (rejects a schedule that is neither 24/7 nor has any window, since it would match nothing; EndMin<=StartMin is explicitly valid and means an overnight/night-shift wrap) plus /api/schedules/holidays CRUD, and GET/POST /api/grants (validates all three legs exist before writing, treats a duplicate grant as a no-op returning the existing row). All writes are admin-only on top of the existing deny-by-default RBAC matrix, mirroring doors.create. Deleting a group or schedule still referenced by a grant is refused in plain words; deleting a group cascades its memberships. Every grant/membership mutation now publishes a named access.rule-change notification to the local feed (and, on an adopted node, up the fleet control channel), directly answering the RBAC doc's warning that a grant edit otherwise 'looks like nothing in a log'. The frontend gains an admin-only Access screen (views/Access.js, lib/access.js) and the first-run wizard now calls ensureDefaultAccess after creating the first person: it builds (or reuses, by name) an Everyone group and an Always 24/7 schedule, adds the person, and grants the group the door the wizard just created, so a fresh install badges successfully the moment setup finishes. Live-bench verified: existing grant -> badge GRANTED; DELETE grant -> next badge DENIED (no-grant); POST grant -> next badge GRANTED again, with named notifications for both mutations; a full headless first-run wizard walk produced the Everyone group, membership and door grant, and reused the pre-existing Always schedule on a second run.
compatibility: Backward compatible. mypintusan still has no entry in infra/versioning/version.json's apps map, so this ships under the core/infra scope and does not cut a mypintusan release or tag. The new endpoints are additive; no schema or migration changes (AccessGroup/Schedule/ScheduleWindow/Holiday/Grant were already part of the 12-table access schema and already persisted via dbsql.NewGenericRepo, only the HTTP surface over them is new). Existing installs with holders and doors already configured are unaffected until an operator (or a fresh wizard run) actually creates a group/schedule/grant; ordinary person creation outside the wizard remains fail-closed as before.
